content: Do not take ramipril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as ramipril can cause harm to the developing fetus. It is also used to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke in individuals at risk for these conditions. Additionally, it improves survival in patients with heart failure following a heart attack. Ramipril belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing certain chemicals in the body that constrict blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and enabling the heart to pump blood more effectively. Ramipril is available as an oral capsule and is typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed; do not take more or less than directed. Swallow the capsule whole, or you may open it and sprinkle the contents onto a small amount of applesauce (approximately 4 ounces) or mix it with 4 ounces of water or apple juice. Consume the entire mixture. If prepared in advance, the mixture can be stored for up to 24 hours at room temperature or 48 hours in the refrigerator. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before starting ramipril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ramipril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, or trandolapril. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Inform your doctor if you have a history of heart, liver, or kidney disease; lupus; scleroderma; diabetes; or angioedema, a condition characterized by swelling and difficulty breathing or swallowing. Notify your doctor if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking ramipril. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Ramipril may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: headache, dizziness, cough, upset stomach, vomiting, fatigue, or weakness. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; yellowing of the skin or eyes; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; lightheadedness; or fainting. If you experience any unusual or severe side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store ramipril in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness or fainting. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking ramipril. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Ramipril is sold under the brand name Altace®.
